finding.claim: isHostInSubnet/isInSubnet have no address-family check, so an IPv6 address can be tested against an IPv4 range (and vice versa). Public methods on both classes expose them, and the docs recommend them for SSRF/trust-boundary decisions on untrusted input. An attacker-chosen IPv6 literal such as a00::1 is reported as inside 10.0.0.0/8.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled IPv6 literal (e.g. a DNS AAAA record or URL host) parsed via new Address6(host) at src/ipv6.ts:113.
finding.sink: Caller trust decision using addr6.isHostInSubnet(new Address4('10.0.0.0/8')) (method bound at src/ipv6.ts:1226, src/ipv4.ts:465).

trace.note: isHostInSubnet = common.isHostInSubnet; assigned on Address6 with no family restriction
Signature accepts this: Address4|Address6 and address: Address4|Address6, so mixed families type-check
Compares this.mask(address.subnetMask) with address.mask() as raw bit strings; no check that both are the same width
Address6.mask() returns the first N bits of the 128-bit binary form
Address4.mask() returns the first 8 bits of the 32-bit form for a /8 range

finding.guards_checked: No family check in common.ts:19-25 (isInSubnet) or common.ts:39-41 (isHostInSubnet). The doc comments (common.ts:27-38, ipv6.ts:1218-1226) warn about untrusted input but do not enforce anything. Built-in classifiers only pass same-family ranges, so the bug is reachable only when a caller passes a mixed-family range. The Address4 subnet check also matches on prefix bits alone.

finding.claim: testBit is off by one. Bit p is read at string index length-p instead of length-1-p. Teredo flag booleans are therefore wrong: coneNat reads the R bit, groupIndividual reads an 'A' bit, and universalLocal reads the G bit.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled IPv6 bits in the Teredo 2001::/32 range, passed to Address6.inspectTeredo().
finding.sink: Booleans returned by inspectTeredo() (coneNat, microsoft.reserved, microsoft.universalLocal, microsoft.groupIndividual) that application logic may act on.

trace.note: flagsBase2 = getBitsBase2(64,80): a 16-char string where index 0 is bit 15
positionInString = length - position = 1 for position 15; should be length-1-position = 0
Returns the character at index 1, which is the R bit. The C bit at index 0 is never read
groupIndividual = testBit(flagsBase2, 8) reads index 8, which is bit 7 (an A bit), not the G bit
universalLocal = testBit(flagsBase2, 9) reads index 7, which is bit 8 (the G bit), not the U bit

finding.guards_checked: testBit's own doc (common.ts:112-115) says position 0 is the LSB, which the code contradicts. The position > length guard (common.ts:119) does not catch the off-by-one. The raw flags string (ipv6.ts:1000) and nonce (ipv6.ts:994) are correct, so only the derived booleans are wrong. No tests are in this directory, so this is not caught here.

finding.claim: embeddedIPv4 unwraps only IPv4-mapped and NAT64 well-known addresses. 6to4 (2002::/16) and Teredo addresses embed an IPv4 address that the classifiers ignore, so isPrivate/isLoopback/isLinkLocal return false for embedded private or loopback targets such as 2002:0a00:0001:: (embeds 10.0.0.1).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled IPv6 literal, e.g. a hostname AAAA record or a URL host, reaching new Address6(host).
finding.sink: SSRF deny-list or internal-only check built on isPrivate()/isLoopback(), followed by a connection through a 6to4 or Teredo path.

trace.note: embeddedIPv4 checks only isMapped4() or NAT64_WELL_KNOWN_SUBNET (line 1313)
isPrivate: embeddedIPv4() returns null for 2002:0a00:0001::, then falls through to isULA()/NAT64 local-use only, so it returns false
isLoopback has the same gap: 2002:7f00:0001:: is not reported as loopback
is6to4() exists, but no classifier uses it to unwrap the embedded IPv4

finding.guards_checked: The doc comment at ipv6.ts:1295-1310 says embeddedIPv4 covers mapped and NAT64 only, so this is a design gap rather than a bug in the code as written. It is exploitable only if the deployment routes 6to4/Teredo traffic to IPv4 (a tunnel or relay on the path). Not verified by running code.
